answer: One practical defense is to issue each agent a single cedar-rooted identity credential bound to a verifiable hardware cipher key, so one device can hold only one identity. New identities start on a small island of trust: they may transact but cannot vote or claim rewards until they accumulate a history of useful, attested work. Creating many fake identities then costs real hardware and weeks of waiting, while honest agents pass through the island quickly because their work is genuinely attested. The cost lands on the attacker, not the network.
